qa_pairs.question: When connecting to a cluster via SSH, how do users provide their second factor for multifactor authentication?
qa_pairs.answer: After entering their password or SSH key, users will be prompted for their second factor. They can approve a Duo Push notification on a smart device, simply touch their YubiKey when the "Passcode" prompt appears, or paste/type a backup code or a time-based one-time password from the Duo Mobile application.

qa_pairs.question: How can Linux and macOS users configure their OpenSSH client to reduce the number of times they are prompted for their second factor during a session?
qa_pairs.answer: Linux and macOS users can reduce the frequency of second factor prompts by editing their `~/.ssh/config` file to include `ControlPath`, `ControlMaster auto`, and `ControlPersist 10m` for a specific host. This configuration allows a first SSH session to handle both authentication factors, while subsequent SSH connections on the same device can reuse this session for up to 10 minutes without requiring re-authentication.
